newsitem.title: USA: High Plains ethanol incentive extended.
newsitem.headline: High Plains ethanol incentive extended.

text.p: High Plains Corp said Friday the Kansas Agricultural Ethanol Production Incentive Program was extended to July 1, 2001. It said the program contributes about $0.08 per gallon to the company's profitability on ethanol produced at its Colwich, Kan. plant.
Earlier, High Plains posted March 31 third quarter earnings of $427,922 or $0.03 per share, down from $950,359 or $0.06 per share a year ago.

President Raymond Friend said, "In this quarter, we were affected by reductions in ethanol prices, higher feedstock costs and some plant production interruptions at our York, Neb. plant which reduced profitability."

"Prices on the portion of ethanol gallons we were unable to pre-sell dropped earlier than normal for the wintertime Oxyfuel season period. Spot prices dropped as low as $1.02, but have now rebounded and appear to have stabilized at approximately $1.10 per gallon," Friend added.
The executive said High Plains' plants are operating at capacity, producing fuel grade ethanol.

"Our engineers are working on process changes for our industrial grade production unit. We expect to begin limited shipments of the industrial grade product by month end, at sales prices which should yield higher net margins than the fuel grade product," Friend said in a statement.
He said the ethanol company is pursuing supply agreements with several potential industrial grade ethanol customers.
